newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down, wet forecast hits new crop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down, wet forecast hits new crop.

text.p: Forecasts for more rain this weekend in the U.S. Midwest and USDA data indicating lackluster weekly export sales led CBOT new crop soybean futures lower on Thursday, traders said.
"With the rains we had last week and the rains that are forecast, we are probably going to have a record crop," said Tim Hannagan, head grain analyst with Alaron Trading Corp.

"The government came out on Tuesday and predicted a 2.7 billion bushel crop," he added. "We've had ample rain falling over the driest areas since then. The trade assumes on the next report they're going to increase it even more.

Forecasts called for widespread weekend rains of 0.25 to 1.50 inch with anywhere from 65 to 80 percent coverage, meteorologists said. That outlook tempered recent concerns about moisture deficiency as soybeans set and fill pods.

USDA weekly export sales data further weakened new crop months. USDA Thursday said U.S. net exports of new crop soybeans during the week ended August 7 totalled 193,800 tonnes, below expectations for 300,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
Soybeans ended 6-1/2 to 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower with November down 3-3/4 at $6.11-3/4 and August off 6-1/2 at $7.72-1/2.

August was up sharply in morning trade amid strong cash basis levels and talk of export demand out of the Great Lakes and U.S. Gulf. But the August fell near midday as commercials sold, dousing theories of strong nearby demand.
"Somebody is buying some soybeans," Hannagan said. "There's beans being shipped out of Chicago. The problem is that somebody can't get them at the elevator so they were buying futures contracts.
There were 40,000 bushels of soybeans posted for delivery against the August on Thursday.
CBOT said the preliminary open interest in the August stood at 28.97 million bushels as of August 13, down 6.345 million from the previous day. The August expires August 20.
On the day, Produce Grain sold 600,000 bushels August and Term Commodities sold 500,000 August, traders said.
Refco Inc sold at least 3.5 million bushels November while Smith Barney sold three million November and Iowa Grain traded 2.5 million November, pit sources said.
Produce Grain, Farmers Commodities Corp and Continental Grain were said to be November/August bear spreaders.
In options trade, Lind-Waldock bought 1,5000 November $6.75 calls at 5-3/4 to six cents, floor sources said.
Rand Financials bought 900 November $6.00 puts and sold 900 November $5.50 puts and 900 November $6.50 calls at six to 4-1/2 cents.
Volatility in the November was pegged at 19-3/4 percent, against 20-3/4 percent on Wednesday.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 44,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 44,591.
